newsitem.title: OMAN: Syrian leader calls on Arabs to pressure Israel.
newsitem.headline: Syrian leader calls on Arabs to pressure Israel.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, on a Gulf tour seeking support for Syria's peace stand, on Wednesday urged Arab states to pressure Israel into abiding by previous peace agreements.

"Does this mean that we are restricted to choosing to surrender to what Israel wants? The alternative is resistance and working to boost Arab and international efforts to pressure Israel into...abiding by agreements reached in past negotiations," he told reporters.
Khaddam was speaking after arriving in Muscat on Wednesday for talks with Sultan Qaboos bin Said as part of a regional tour.

He was accompanied by Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on a tour to drum up support for Syria's peace stand after Israel and the PLO settled their deadlock on the West Bank town of Hebron earlier this month, Gulf Arab newspapers have said.

They arrived from Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where Khaddam brushed aside Israeli suggestions their bilateral Middle East peace talks are about to resume after a 10-month break.
They have also been to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
"There is no movement until now regarding resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he said after talks with UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan late on Tuesday.
"The Israeli media campaign expressing optimism regarding restarting talks aims at misleading public opinion," he added in remarks carried by the UAE official WAM news agency.
